title: Ordinary scalar insertion reduced to common quotients
statement: For g:J→K preserving finite limits, normalized ordinary scalar extensions nY and nX, R→B and a:g(B)→Bprime, and a common quotient tower Q of R→B, suppose b:Bprime→g(Q.S) is compatible with a and makes each square for g(R)→Bprime a common quotient. If an ordinary natural transformation from inverse image of restriction to restriction of scalar extension along a sends x to 1 tensor the underlying inverse-image section, then its scalar extension to g(Q.S_n) is invertible for every n. This uses no flatness, complex or derived-category hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 06YY (derived base change), 0G7E (K-flat pullback), 0D6D (composition); sites-modules.tex Tags 03D7, 03EK, 03EL.

proof.text: A locally-surjective quotient is an epimorphism of underlying sheaves. Left adjoint inverse image preserves that epimorphism, and the ring-underlying isomorphisms transport it to g(Q.projection n). Thus the assumed target pushout and b define a common quotient tower on K.

The ordinary common-quotient tower comparison identifies restriction followed by scalar extension with scalar extension along the second projection, with s tensor x preserved. Convert its cochain-model scalar extensions to the normalized scalar extensions through their specified object and morphism equations.

Apply that comparison on J and K. Transport the J comparison through exact inverse image using the ordinary coefficient tensor comparison; compose the K comparison with scalar associativity along a and b. These give two natural isomorphisms from the reduced source and target to the same g(Q.S_n)-module functor.

The coefficient comparison insertion equation, naturality of moduleUnderlying, and the common-quotient section formula identify the first isomorphism on the quotient unit. The second identifies iterated unit insertion with the composite unit by normalized scalar associativity. The adjunction hom equivalence and faithfulness of underlying sheaves therefore identify extension of the given insertion followed by the second isomorphism with the first. Cancel the second isomorphism to obtain invertibility.

theorem ordinary_insertion_reduction_isIso [PreservesFiniteLimits uInv]
    (hquotient : ∀ n : ℕ, IsPushout (g.rings.map φ ≫ a)
      (quotient g φ Q n) (b.app (op n)) (𝟙 _))
    (hcompatible : ∀ n : ℕ, a ≫ b.app (op n) = g.rings.map (Q.extensionProjection n))
    (δ : ordinarySource g φ ⟶ ordinaryTarget g (pX := pX) φ a)
    (hδ : ∀ (M : Mod J B) (U : Xᵒᵖ)
      (x : ((g.inverse R).modules.obj ((restriction φ).obj M)).val.obj U),
      (δ.app M).val.app U x = sectionTensor (pX a) ((g.inverse B).modules.obj M) U 1
        (((g.inverse R).moduleUnderlying.hom.app ((restriction φ).obj M) ≫
          (g.inverse B).moduleUnderlying.inv.app M).hom.app U x))
    (n : ℕ) : IsIso (Functor.whiskerRight δ (pX (quotient g φ Q n)).ordinary)
